subject.title: fix(process): trim UTF-8 boundary on win32 in truncated command output

question: Should truncated Windows child-process output be treated as guaranteed UTF-8 and normalized at capture time, or must OpenClaw preserve arbitrary raw Windows command bytes?
rationale: The correct fix depends on the supported encoding contract for external Windows commands; tests using Node UTF-8 output cannot choose that compatibility policy.

options.title: Preserve raw Windows output
options.body: Keep the existing Windows bypass and close or rework this PR unless a broader encoding contract is intentionally adopted.

options.title: Adopt an explicit UTF-8 contract
options.body: Approve a documented, encoding-aware capture design with native Windows proof for UTF-8 and legacy-code-page command output before removing the guard.

recommendation.title: Preserve raw Windows output
recommendation.body: Keep the existing Windows bypass and close or rework this PR unless a broader encoding contract is intentionally adopted.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior dates to an earlier process-output refactor, but the available history context cannot safely identify its author.
